response.text:
Evidence supports testing more negatives before changing SASRec’s architecture. [gSASRec (IJCAI 2024)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) identifies overconfidence from sampled BCE and introduces generalized BCE; its [extended abstract](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) recommends 128–256 negatives and calibration parameter t=0.75, balancing effectiveness against computation. These are useful experimental starting points, not established optima for this benchmark. Compare single-negative BCE, multi-negative BCE/gBCE, and sampled-softmax cross-entropy under comparable GPU budgets; increasing negative count alone does not correct sampling bias.

Hardness needs scheduling and false-negative controls. [R²NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) combines uniform-sampling warm-up, global candidate recall, and progressively harder stochastic top-M selection; it reports that introducing hard negatives too early can underperform uniform sampling. [CATS (SIGIR 2026)](https://iris.uniroma1.it/handle/11573/1775773) adaptively samples across item clusters while reducing sampling from the positive item’s own cluster, motivated by false-negative risk. Practical inference: first test uniform multi-negative objectives; then mix uniform and moderately hard negatives after warm-up, excluding known training positives and avoiding deterministic hardest-only selection. Use learned interaction embeddings for optional similarity controls; similarity does not establish a true false negative. Select by the prescribed four-category macro validation HR@10 and inspect Electronics separately. Larger diagnostic margins or published gains on other datasets do not establish improvement under this evaluator.
